a: Gitnetix is a release-centric Git client for macOS, Windows and Linux. Instead of a commit graph, it shows your branches as a tree: main, then releases, then the features and fixes that belong to them. It ships a release in one click and can run an AI agent on every branch.

Yes. Gitnetix is free to download and use on macOS, Windows and Linux, and updates itself. AI features run through your own signed-in CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot) or an API key, so any AI cost goes to your provider, and local models through Ollama cost nothing.

q: How is it different from other Git GUIs?
a: Most Git clients are built around the commit graph, which shows what git stored. Gitnetix drops it and shows intent: which release a branch belongs to, what is still open, what shipped and what is falling behind. It works out each branch's real parent, even after a squash-merged pull request.

q: Can I still see a commit graph?
a: Yes, when you want one. A Graph column opens beside the branches, limited to the branch you're on, where it started and a few around it. Hover an action (rebase, merge, push, tag, reset) and it shows your branches as they will be once it's done, before you click.

q: Is Gitnetix an alternative to GitKraken, Fork or Sourcetree?
a: Yes. Like GitKraken, Fork, Sourcetree, Tower or GitHub Desktop, it is a desktop Git GUI for everyday branching, committing, merging and pull requests. The difference is the picture: those clients are built around the commit graph, while Gitnetix shows branches as a tree of releases and the work inside them, with a one-click release flow and an AI agent per branch.

q: Which AI agents does it work with?
a: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot and Ollama through their signed-in CLIs, or any provider with an API key. You pick the provider, model and effort for each agent session, and each one runs in its branch's own worktree.

q: Does it support GitLab or Bitbucket?
a: Not yet. Any git remote works for branches, commits and releases. Pull request features currently cover GitHub and Azure DevOps.

q: macOS says Gitnetix "is damaged". Is it safe?
a: The app is fine. It isn't notarized yet, so macOS can't check who made it. After moving it to Applications, run xattr -cr /Applications/Gitnetix.app once. If that says "Permission denied", copy it to ~/Applications and clear the flag there (commands on the Download page). Or choose Open Anyway in System Settings › Privacy & Security. Updates from inside the app don't need this again.

q: Can I manage it from my phone?
a: Yes. Scan the QR code shown by your desktop (or a headless server) and Gitnetix opens in your phone's browser, no app store needed. From there you can drive releases, agents, worktrees, pull requests and tickets.
